# Intake & Durable Queue Requirements Quality Checklist: 002-intake-queue

**Purpose**: Validate the *quality* of the 002-intake-queue requirements — completeness, clarity,
consistency, measurability, and coverage — before implementation. These are "unit tests for the
requirements," not tests of behaviour.
**Created**: 2026-11-03
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) (see also [plan.md](../plan.md), [data-model.md](../data-model.md))

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: Reviewer-owned requirements-quality artifact. A checked box (`[x]`) means a
reviewer judged the requirement-quality criterion satisfied — it does **not** mean code is done.
`/speckit-implement` reads checklist state but never edits these markers. Items are generated unchecked.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Is each inbound source's identifier provenance (email / web / api) fully specified, or only given by example? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are all request lifecycle states enumerated (`received`, `processing`, `awaiting_pipeline`, `needs_review`) with every transition between them specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008/§FR-011]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are the fields a status lookup returns for a request defined? [Gap, Spec §FR-008/§US4]
- [x] CHK004 - Is the maximum content size and the full set of required submission fields specified at the requirement level (not only in the contract)? [Gap, Spec §FR-012] — Resolved 2026-11-03: FR-012 now pins ≤20,000 chars, deterministic rejection, consistent with the contract.
- [ ] CHK005 - Is the stuck-work deadline specified as bounded/configurable with a stated basis (above worst-case run), rather than left vague? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the retry attempt cap (how many attempts before parking in `needs_review`) specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-011] — Resolved 2026-11-03: FR-011 sets a default of 3 total attempts (incl. first), configurable, single retry authority.
- [ ] CHK007 - Is behaviour specified for a partially-failed atomic write (what the client observes and may safely do)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [ ] CHK008 - Is "same content" vs "different content" defined precisely enough (canonicalization rule) to decide replay vs `409` without ambiguity? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005/§FR-006]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is "immediate acknowledgement before any background processing begins" objectively verifiable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-003/§SC-001]
- [x] CHK010 - Is "a bounded number of attempts" quantified or given a definite basis? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011] — Resolved 2026-11-03: quantified as default 3 total attempts (incl. first); see FR-011 / SC-005.
- [ ] CHK011 - Is "stable source submission identifier" defined with constraints (what makes it stable; uniqueness scope)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK012 - Can "no accepted message is ever lost" be objectively verified as written? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011/§SC-005]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is the worker's deterministic "processing step" for this slice defined (what it does, given there is no AI)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009/§FR-013]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK014 - Is the idempotency-key tuple named consistently (shop/tenant, source/namespace, submission id) across requirements, entities, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is the terminal-for-002 state named `awaiting_pipeline` consistently across requirements, entities, success criteria, and clarifications? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK016 - Do "return the existing request" (FR-005) and "409 conflict" (FR-006) partition the same-key space with no overlap or gap? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005/§FR-006]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is "`202 Accepted`" (HTTP status) consistently distinguished from the internal `awaiting_pipeline` state wherever acknowledgement is described? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK018 - Are isolation requirements consistent with 001 (shop from credential, forced RLS) with no contradicting statement? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001/§FR-014]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK019 - Does every P1/P2 user story (US1–US4) carry at least one objectively verifiable acceptance scenario? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §US1–US4]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are SC-001–SC-008 each tied to a verifiable condition free of implementation detail? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-008]
- [ ] CHK021 - Is there a measurable criterion separating replay (identical content) from conflict (different content) under the same identifier? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-002/§SC-003]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is the concurrent-duplicate outcome ("exactly one request") stated as a measurable criterion? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-002]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 - Is the primary flow (submit → acknowledge → background completion) fully specified? [Coverage, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK024 - Are alternate flows specified: identical replay, and different-identifier/identical-content? [Coverage, Spec §US2/§FR-015]
- [ ] CHK025 - Are exception flows specified for each rejection class (missing identifier, oversized, malformed, conflict)? [Exception Flow, Spec §FR-004/§FR-006/§FR-012]
- [ ] CHK026 - Are recovery flows specified for worker crash, lost queue contents, and poison work? [Recovery, Spec §FR-010/§FR-011]
- [ ] CHK027 - Is "rebuild pending work from request state" stated as a requirement, not only an assumption? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK028 - Is the same-key/same-content concurrent duplicate explicitly addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK029 - Is behaviour specified when a submission supplies no source submission identifier? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-004/§FR-015]
- [ ] CHK030 - Is a whitespace/formatting-only difference under a reused identifier addressed so it does not produce a false `409`? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK031 - Is a cross-tenant request-id status lookup addressed (not found for a non-owner)? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-014/§SC-006]
- [ ] CHK032 - Is premature sweeping of still-in-flight work addressed (the deadline bound)? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK033 - Are customer replies (own identifier, correlated not deduped) addressed as a boundary even though built later? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK034 - Are reliability requirements (no-loss, bounded retries, visible failure) stated measurably? [NFR, Spec §FR-011/§SC-005]
- [x] CHK035 - Is the requirement that customer message content is never logged stated at the spec/requirement level (not only the plan/constitution)? [Gap, Principle VII] — Resolved 2026-11-03: new FR-018 + SC-009 prohibit logging content/email/credentials; only safe metadata.
- [ ] CHK036 - Are isolation requirements for the new data (messages / requests / jobs) stated at the requirement level? [Security, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK037 - Is the intake authentication requirement (shop credential; shop from credential) explicit and consistent with 001? [Security, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK038 - Is any intake throughput/latency expectation stated, or explicitly declared out of scope for this slice? [NFR, Gap]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK039 - Is the dependency on 001 (auth, forced RLS, roles, config) documented? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK040 - Is the queue technology (pg-boss) correctly deferred to planning rather than pinned in the spec? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK041 - Is the canonical-payload comparison rule documented as a plan-level assumption with a definite basis? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK042 - Are out-of-scope boundaries (no AI, orders, pricing, email, web UI, semantic dedup) explicitly declared? [Scope, Spec §FR-013/§FR-015]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK043 - Is the spec free of residual text implying content-based deduplication (which would conflict with FR-015)? [Conflict, Spec §FR-015] — Verified 2026-11-03: no content-dedup requirement remains; FR-015 now states only same-identifier/same-tenant/same-source submissions are dedup-eligible, fingerprint is conflict-detection only.
- [ ] CHK044 - Is "tracking reference" disambiguated from "request id" (same thing, named once)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003/§US4]
- [ ] CHK045 - Are the actors (submitting client, worker, relay, sweeper, operator) disambiguated wherever responsibilities are assigned? [Ambiguity]
- [ ] CHK046 - Is a requirement/acceptance-criteria ID scheme (FR/SC/US) established and used consistently so every item is traceable? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Scope selected: **Comprehensive intake-queue** (idempotency & dedup, durable-queue reliability/
  recovery, request state machine, tenant isolation, privacy, scope/contract clarity). Depth:
  **Standard→gate** (the constitution treats "no accepted message is ever lost" and isolation as gates).
  Audience/timing: **PR reviewer**, before `/speckit-tasks` / implementation.
- Traceability: 43 of 46 items carry a spec reference or an explicit `[Gap]`/`[Assumption]`/`[Conflict]`
  marker (>80%); the few unreferenced are cross-cutting (actor disambiguation, throughput-scope, ID scheme).
- These items test the *requirements*, not the system. A few likely-true `[Gap]` candidates to weigh:
  CHK004 (content-size limit lives in the contract, not a spec FR), CHK006/CHK010 (attempt cap not
  quantified), CHK035 (no-log-content stated in plan/constitution, not the spec FR). Resolve any real
  gap by editing the spec (optionally via `/speckit-clarify`) before implementation.
